title: Path Parameters
summary: Declare path parameters with type validation, enum support, and path converters.

sections.content: What Are Path Parameters?
Path parameters are values extracted from the URL path. You declare them using curly braces {} in the route path, and FastAPI extracts and validates them automatically.
Here {user_id} is a path parameter. The type annotation int drives validation — if the client sends /users/abc, FastAPI returns a 422 error automatically.
Ordering Matters (Static First)
FastAPI matches routes in declaration order. Static routes must be declared before parameterized routes that would match the same pattern:

sections.title: Common bug
sections.content: If /users/{user_id} is declared first, /users/me will match it with user_id="me". Always put static paths before parameterized ones.
Enum Path Parameters
Use Python enums to restrict path parameters to a fixed set of values. FastAPI validates the input and renders a dropdown in the docs UI.
Values outside the enum automatically get a 422 error.
Path Converter (Regex)
The :path converter allows slashes in the parameter value, useful for file paths:

sections.title: Security: path traversal
sections.content: The :path converter can match ../ segments. Always sanitize or reject .. segments if the value touches your filesystem.
Path Parameter Validation
Use Path() to add constraints and metadata to path parameters:
Constraints: ge (>=), gt (>), le (<=), lt (<). Violations return 422 with per-field messages.

code_challenge.title: Path Parameters with Validation
code_challenge.description: Create an app with GET /users/{user_id} that validates user_id as a positive integer. Also add GET /users/me that returns {"user_id": "current"}.
code_challenge.starter_code:
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

# TODO: Add GET /users/me (must be before /users/{user_id})

# TODO: Add GET /users/{user_id} with int type hint
hints: Use user_id: int as the type annotation
The int type annotation gives you validation for free

quiz.question: What does {user_id} in the path /users/{user_id} declare?
quiz.explanation: Curly braces {} in the URL path declare a path parameter. FastAPI extracts the value and validates it against the type annotation.

quiz.question: Why must /users/me be declared before /users/{user_id}?
options: FastAPI matches routes in declaration order
quiz.explanation: FastAPI evaluates routes in the order they're declared. If /users/{user_id} comes first, 'me' matches as the parameter value.

quiz.question: What happens when you send /users/abc to a route with user_id: int?
quiz.explanation: The int type annotation drives validation. 'abc' can't be parsed as an integer, so FastAPI returns 422 Unprocessable Entity.

quiz.question: What does the :path converter do?
options: Allows slashes in the parameter value
quiz.explanation: The :path converter ({file_path:path}) allows the parameter to contain slashes, matching the rest of the URL.

quiz.question: How do you add a minimum value constraint to a path parameter?
quiz.explanation: Use Path(ge=1) in the type annotation: item_id: Annotated[int, Path(ge=1)]. This adds validation automatically.
